The little clock does the same job — clicking it queued the article and the toast confirmed it — so it works. But comparing the two, the clearly labeled button is the more natural one for me. With the plain clock, I'd have to guess what it means the first few times, or hover and hope; the button that actually says "Read later," then flips to "In Read later," leaves no doubt about what it does or whether I've already marked something. Since this isn't an action I do constantly, I'd rather it spell itself out than save a little space.

So my pick is the labeled button, version A. The icon's a fine compact option if space ever gets tight, but for me the words win.
